areas_of_law: Aboriginal and treaty rights / constitutional law
Tax Court of Canada procedure (motions to strike)
Crown-Indigenous fiduciary duty / duty to consult
issues: Whether it is plain and obvious that the pleaded constitutional and inherent-rights arguments disclose no reasonable basis to succeed, warranting striking the appeals/notice of constitutional question
Whether the Tax Court of Canada has jurisdiction to consider constitutional and Aboriginal/inherent-rights arguments raised in an income tax appeal

Whether employment income earned off-reserve through a placement agency serving urban Indigenous organizations can be 'situated on a reserve' under the connecting-factors test for the s.87 Indian Act tax exemption
Whether taxation of status Indians' off-reserve employment income breaches s.35 Aboriginal or treaty rights absent historical consent or a constitutional conference
Whether the Crown owes a fiduciary duty or duty to consult specifically in relation to the general taxation of status Indians' off-reserve income
Whether taxing off-reserve earnings of status Indians differently from on-reserve earnings constitutes discrimination under s.15 of the Charter
Whether taxation of off-reserve income infringes mobility or livelihood rights under s.6 of the Charter
What pleading and evidentiary standard applies to self-represented litigants on a motion to strike constitutional pleadings in tax litigation
key_facts: Both clients are registered status Indians and members of First Nations
They lived and worked off-reserve in a large city during the years in issue
Employment was through a placement agency hiring out Indigenous workers to urban social service organizations
One worked part-time as an Indigenous support worker; the other at an Indigenous legal clinic
Employment income was not reported to the tax authority
CRA reassessed on the basis the income was not situated on a reserve, so the s.87 Indian Act exemption did not apply
Appellants are self-represented and filed appeals plus a notice of constitutional question

Arguments raised include lack of Indigenous consent to taxation, lack of consultation, absence of a constitutional conference, breach of fiduciary duty/duty to consult, discrimination against off-reserve workers, interference with right to earn a living, and lack of Tax Court jurisdiction over inherent rights
The Crown has brought a motion to strike the appeals and the constitutional notice as disclosing no reasonable prospect of success
causes_of_action: Appeal of tax reassessment under the Income Tax Act
Claim that employment income is situated on a reserve and exempt under s.87 of the Indian Act
Constitutional challenge to taxation of off-reserve income under s.35 Aboriginal rights
Alleged breach of Crown fiduciary duty and duty to consult regarding taxation
Alleged Charter s.15 discrimination and s.6 mobility/right-to-earn-a-living infringement
candidate_statutes: Tax Court of Canada Rules (General Procedure), Rule 53
Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, s. 15
Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, s. 6
